episodes.164358: The first of two strong Pacific fronts brought high winds to the coast as well as gusty winds to the Willamette Valley and interior lowlands of southwest Washington. This storm generated large seas impacting the coastline, and combined with rising river levels and high astronomical tides, resulted in some flooding along the coast due to poor drainage.  In addition to the wind and rain, heavy snow fell in the mountains and in the Columbia River Gorge where  transportation corridors between western and eastern Oregon and Washington were temporarily closed due the heavy snow accumulation.
episodes.164627: Numerous showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front brought severe weather to the tri-state area.  Several reports of trees and power lines blown down were received from across the region along with one tornado in Walton county, FL.
episodes.164628: Numerous showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front brought severe weather to the tri-state area.  Several reports of trees and power lines blown down were received from across the region along with one tornado in Walton county, FL.
episodes.164629: Numerous showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front brought strong thunderstorms to the coastal waters.  Several gusts were measured in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.164819: A surface trough moving from the southeast and south, and an upper low far west of the islands created instability statewide.  These features produced heavy showers and thunderstorms over portions of the state.  Rainfall was particularly intense over parts of Oahu, Kauai, and the Big Island which led to flash flooding.  There were no reports of serious injuries.  The costs of any damages were not available.  This episode is a continuation from the end of December.
episodes.164952: A cold front and line of storms moved across the west Florida coastal waters during the early morning producing multiple strong marine wind gusts.
episodes.165118: A potent shortwave became negatively tilted and dug east across the deep south which drove a strong cold front across the local area during the late afternoon and early evening hours. Strong to severe thunderstorms consolidated into a squall line that moved from western inland SE GA and the Suwannee valley east-southeast through the |I-10 and I-75 corridors to the Atlantic coast through midnight. A very strong low level jet of 50-60 knots with CAPE of at least 500 J/kg to brought some damaging wind gusts of across SE GA.
episodes.165130: A strong upper level low moved from the Midwest into the Mid Atlantic from January 2nd into the 3rd. Strong storms to isolated severe storms preceded the arrival of the low along with a broad area of 2 to 4 inches of rain along United States Highway 1 corridor, producing flooding around the Triangle region of central North Carolina. Strong sustained gradient winds were felt over much of the area, with numerous gusts of 35 to 50 miles per hour. As the low moved through the area, rain mixed with and changed to snow with several inches of snow reported across portions of the northwest and far northern Piedmont.
episodes.165203: A strong cold front resulted in a band of severe thunderstorms and strong gradient winds across portions of northeast SC and southeast NC.
episodes.165204: A strong cold front resulted in a band of severe thunderstorms and strong gradient winds across portions of northeast SC and southeast NC.
episodes.165206: A strong cold front resulted in strong gradient winds across portions of the adjacent coastal waters.
episodes.165357: A series of heavy rainfall events in late December and early January sent the Wabash, White, and portions of the Ohio River above flood stage. The river flooding was minor. Low-lying farmland and fields along both rivers were flooded, as well as some river access roads and public recreational land.
episodes.165748: An area of low pressure developing across the Southeast strengthened and lifted a warm front across southeast Georgia in the late evening hours. Along the front, a line of thunderstorms developed and impacted portions of southeast Georgia. One storm became severe in Tattnall County and produced wind damage near Reidsville, GA.
episodes.166078: Heavy rain brought flooding to some rivers in northeast Arkansas January 1-3, 2022.
episodes.166297: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced isolated gale-force wind gusts near the Lower Keys of Monroe County.
episodes.166301: Showers and thunderstorms affected much of the area ahead of a strong storm system and associated cold front. Some of the storms became severe with damaging winds and a few tornadoes, mainly on January 2nd. In the colder air behind the front, rain mixed with and eventually changed over to snow across parts of north Georgia (generally north of I-20/I-85) late on the 2nd and into January 3rd, with a dusting to up to 4 inches of snowfall (mainly across the higher elevations of far north GA). On the back side of this storm system, strong post-frontal winds of 30-50 mph occurred during the early morning hours of January 3rd. Numerous reports of downed trees and powerlines occurred with several injuries.
episodes.166385: Thunderstorms developed and moved through Eastern NC during the morning hours. A few storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts across the region. Strong non-thunderstorm wind gusts developed in the afternoon behind a rapidly strengthening low pressure system that moved across the Outer Banks.
